---
title: "Worked analyses"
subtitle: "One analysis per page, from the call you type to the sentence you write"
toc: false
---

Each page in this section runs one analysis end to end on data that ships with
the package. You see the figure first, then the code that produced it, then the
output it prints, then the claims that output licenses. Everything on a page is
reproducible: the code you read is the code that ran, and each page comes with a
companion script that reruns it in your own session.

These pages give you just enough to run and report each analysis; the Guide
carries the reasoning, the Reference the details.

## The series

1. **[Your first network](../guide/getting-started.qmd).** Install `bgms`, fit
   your first model, and read the network split by evidence. Afterwards you can
   fit [`bgm()`](../reference/bgm.qmd) to your own data and produce the figure
   this site treats as the canonical result display.
2. **[From estimation to evidence](estimation-to-evidence.qmd).** The full
   Wenchuan network, estimated first and then weighed pair by pair with an
   inclusion Bayes factor. Afterwards you
   can say which associations your data support, which they rule out, and which
   they leave open.
3. **[Reading the output](reading-the-output.qmd).** The `summary()` of a real
   fit, walked block by block. Afterwards you can tell whether a fit is
   trustworthy and where every number you need lives.
4. **[Check your priors](check-your-priors.qmd).**
   [`prior_sensitivity_check()`](../reference/prior-sensitivity.qmd)
   run on a fitted model, with its report and its curve read in full. Afterwards
   you can answer the question of whether your prior drove your conclusions, and
   report the answer.
5. **[Comparing groups](comparing-groups.qmd).** Two groups compared with
   [`bgmCompare()`](../reference/bgmCompare.qmd). Afterwards you can state both
   kinds of claim the method separates: this association differs between groups,
   and this one is credibly the same.
6. **[Edge clustering](edge-clustering.qmd).** The stochastic block model prior
   on the same data. Afterwards you can report clusters of variables together
   with the uncertainty in the allocations.
7. **[Coming from bootnet and qgraph](from-bootnet-qgraph.qmd).** Your current
   workflow mapped onto `bgms`, call by call. Afterwards you know which function
   replaces which step, what is new, and what has no direct analogue.
8. **Reporting your results.** Checklists and template paragraphs per analysis
   type. Afterwards you can assemble a Methods and Results section that a
   reviewer can follow.

Entries without a link are still in preparation.

## How to use a page

Read the figure and the opening question first: they tell you whether the page
answers the question you arrived with. The code chunks are shown in the order
they ran, so you can work through a page from top to bottom in your own session.
Where a page needs the reasoning behind a choice, it links to the
[Guide](../guide/index.qmd); where it needs an argument, a default, or a return
value, it links to the [Reference](../reference/index.qmd).
